speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked	the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) what is the line-up of major sporting events 	to be held at the Sports Hub for this year ; (b) whether pricing is an issue why the Sports Hub is not attracting more bookings; and (c) what is the Government doing to attract more iconic international sporting events to be held at the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We share the high expectations that Singaporeans have for the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We want to see the Sports Hub succeed as the integrated sports and lifestyle destination that we envisioned.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We pay 	Page: 21 close attention to all the issues and to the concerns raised by the public and stakeholders regarding the running of the Sports Hub and its events line-up.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Nonetheless, we also recognise that Sports Hub is still in its start-up phase, being in operation for less than two years.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The operators are finding their feet, sorting out the operational problems and understanding the costs of operations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: SHPL has acknowledged the challenges faced and, with our regular feedback, is continuously looking to improve its operations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will give SHPL some time and room to respond to the feedback of stakeholders and the public.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As a national icon, the success of the Sports Hub is a key priority for us in MCCY.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To this end, SportSG is working closely with SHPL and keeping a close watch on the Sports Hub events calendar.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The Minister said we need to give them more time.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: It has been two years already since the Sports Hub was operational.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: When we say give them more time, how many more years do we need to give, for us to see that there are more activities coming up?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Given the scale of the project, I am not sure what was the investment put in by the consortium, but what are their expected returns in the first place?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: As a result, are we having problems in terms of pricing and is that the reason why we are not attracting all these programmes?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Is it because of price or is it because of some other factors?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is an early time, early stage of operations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As Members will recall, 2015 saw several major sporting events, like the SEA Games and the ASEAN Para Games (APG).

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These took place for the first time ever in this new national stadium and also it was the first time for us to hold such large-scale events.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, will these be repeated in the following years?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think we should really give them time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It seems to be shaping up well, although there is still a lot to be done and that is the reason why we are keeping a very close dialogue with the Sports Hub management.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As to whether the pricing is a result of expected returns or not, this is not something that matters to MCCY.

speaker: Mr David Ong (Bukit Batok)
text: A high rental cost has always been a point of contention between the event organisers and Sports Hub Pte Ltd.

speaker: Mr David Ong (Bukit Batok)
text: What more can be done by the Ministry to make this public-private partnership (PPP) work, to better align public service needs as well as private sector ones?

speaker: Mr David Ong (Bukit Batok)
text: The second question is: although it is still early days, what kind of engagement does the Ministry have with Sports Hub Pte Ltd and will it review the current PPP arrangement with Sports Hub, especially for national icons, such as the National Stadium?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As to rental cost, I think the concern is well noted and without the privilege of having information on private negotiations between SHPL and the event organisers, we are not in a position to make specific comments about the cost faced by the event organisers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We would like to look at the entire offering, what they have managed to secure, what they are bringing to us across all segments of the public that we are trying to cater to.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I can assure Members that discussions between SportSG and SHPL are taking place very regularly.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I would say that it is something that the Ministry is also watching very closely.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I can assure Members that we are very, very well engaged with SHPL.
